name: Ziff Davis, Inc.
strengths: June 2026 sale of Connectivity to Accenture for $1.2B left Q3 cash at $1.41B, net cash over $500M.
YTD buybacks of ~$265M cut the share count nearly 14%; Q3 adjusted EPS held at $1.39 vs $1.40.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $82.2M (28.4% margin); RetailMeNot September app commissions rose 25%.
weaknesses: Q3 revenue fell 5.6% to $289.3M, with all four continuing segments down year over year.
Q3 operating loss of $33.6M included a $29.6M Tech & Shopping goodwill charge and a $6.4M asset write-down.
Organic Google referrals dropped ~37% YoY in Q3 and more than 50% over two years, pressuring ads.
opportunities: Q4 revenue guided to double-digit sequential growth; adjusted EPS seen slightly higher YoY on buybacks.
Content was cited 2.7B times in generative-AI features in Q3, nearly 10x Google Search clicks.
Ample cash for buybacks or M&A; management is still weighing portfolio monetization to unlock per-share value.
threats: Q4 revenue is still expected to decline low- to mid-single digits YoY, similar to Q3's drop.
Search and LLM disruption remains a structural ad-traffic headwind with no near-term inflection given.
Most of the remaining ~$145M Connectivity-sale tax bill is due by Q1 2027; more write-downs are possible.
threatNote: No near-term binary event. Q3 results and the Q4 outlook were released Nov 5–6, 2026. Data providers estimate the next report (Q4 2026) for Feb 22, 2027. A Nov 17 RBC conference appearance is not a binary catalyst. The Q3 10-Q says pending legal matters are not likely to have a material adverse effect on the overall financial position, results, or cash flows. Impairments are performance-related, not a restatement or governance issue. Q4 outlook of a further low- to mid-single-digit YoY revenue decline is a soft guide, not a formal full-year guidance cut.
decisionNote: SWOT supports keeping the $46.65 paper buy order: threats are already-disclosed structural headwinds, not a reason to cancel before the order expires.
